channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports Mia Bieniemy, the wife of Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy, was shot Sunday night at the couple’s home in Virginia.
item.description: Mia Bieniemy is reportedly in stable condition and was treated for “serious injuries,” according to police in Loudon County, Virginia. The shooting reportedly took place around 7:00 p.m ET, and Elijah Bieniemy, the son of Eric and Mia, is reportedly being charged with three feloniesthat include use of a firearm in the commission of a felony, malicious wounding, and discharging a firearm within a building. Elijah Bieniemy was reportedly arraigned on Monday morning. Eric Bieniemy was already with the Chiefs in Missouri during the team’s training camp, and the Chiefs did release a statement saying they were aware of the incident. Our thoughts are with the Bieniemy family.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Commanders fired TEs coach Ben Steele.
item.description: According to The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala, Steele was arrested on suspicion of DWI on June 7th and is also facing charges for refusing blood/breath tests and obstructing or resisting an officer without force. Steele was hired by the Commanders in February and spent time with head coach Dan Quinn in Atlanta from 2019-2020.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Patriots HC Mike Vrabel said the team is “very confident in where (A.J. Brown) is at physically.”
item.description: Speaking with the media on Monday, Vrabel said he thinks “a lot of things get fabricated, and people tell stories,” when asked about Brown’s knee. Patriots executive VP of player personnel Elliot Wolf said last month that Brown has managed a degenerative knee condition in one of his knees since he first entered the league, and he has appeared in 15 or more games in three of his last four seasons. Vrabel acknowledged that Brown won’t do “every single thing” in camp/practice, but the team doesn’t appear overly concerned about the recently acquired receiver. Brown has posted four straight 1,000-yard campaigns and has scored seven or more touchdowns in each of those seasons. He profiles as a fringe WR1/WR2 for fantasy purposes in his first season with Drake Maye.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (shin) resumed practicing at training camp on Friday.
item.description: Per The Tacoma News Tribune’s Gregg Bell, Horton is already “running smoothly” in his return from a November 2025 shin injury. That said, the Seahawks are still limiting his reps. Through the first two practices, he worked with QB Sam Darnold in group drills and fielded punts from P Michael Dickson before observing 11-on-11 drills. On Sunday, he spent time running routes with a trainer while his teammates ran 7-on-7s. Hopefully, the rest of his ramp-up period goes smoothly.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: The Tacoma News Tribune’s Gregg Bell reports that Seahawks RB Jadarian Price is being targeted “a lot” in passing drills through the first three days of training camp.
item.description: Per Bell, Seahawks coaches are “maximizing” Price’s reps. He’s played on the first-, second- and third-team offenses in 11-on-11 drills thus far. If Price hopes to smash his fantasy football ADP, earning a role in the passing game sure would help. Although he is an accomplished runner and returner, he has just 15 receptions on his college resumé. We’ll continue to monitor Price’s progress in the coming days and weeks. Stay tuned.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen stood out at training camp on Sunday.
item.description: Chiefs rookies reported for training camp on July 24, and although most veterans do not report until July 28, quarterbacks arrive early, allowing rookies to take reps with QB Patrick Mahomes. Per Taylor, Allen and Mahomes linked up for one of Sunday’s highlights, a touchdown pass thrown to the back of the end zone in 7-on-7 drills. Taylor notes that coach Andy Reid “spent a few minutes giving Allen one-on-one coaching between repetitions, too.” Is this groundbreaking news? No. But, it is positive. The fifth-round rookie was a worthwhile late-round dart throw in dynasty rookie drafts this spring, and is a player to keep an eye on this summer.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Patriots placed EDGE Gabe Jacas on the reserve/NFI list.
item.description: Jacas has not yet practiced with his new team. He underwent a cleanup procedure in his knee and, in what feels like a very related note from ESPN’s Mike Reiss, the Patriots did include an injury waiver on his knee for his rookie contract. That’s a very unusual thing, though perhaps it’s the reason Jacas remained unsigned into training camp. Hopefully, he can begin practicing soon.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison sat out 11-on-11 red zone drills after suffering an apparent injury on Sunday.
item.description: A couple of Cardinals beat reporters chimed in on this one, but the situation is still a little fuzzy. It appears as though Harrison may have tweaked his back, but in a videopostedby ESPN’s Josh Weinfuss, Harrison can be seen pointing to his left ankle when he initially met with the Cardinals’ training staff. After that, Harrison did seem to focus his efforts on hisback, walking around while attempting to stretch it out, at times “grimacing as he bends backward” and even attempting a yoga cobra pose on the sideline — not kidding. The Cardinals have the day off tomorrow and resume practicing on Tuesday. If we do not get an update before then, his participation that day will at least tell us something. Hopefully, this is a non-issue.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: 49ers CB Nate Hobbs did not practice on Sunday.
item.description: Hobbs’ one-off season with the Packers was derailed by a recurring knee injury. Hopefully, this isn’t the same issue. He currently projects as a second-stringer. 49ers backup OT Vederian Lowe left practice early with an apparent right ankle issue.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Nick Wagoner reports that 49ers RB Jordan James “appears to be” the team’s RB2 right now.
item.description: Wagoner said he saw “some good stuff” from James as a rusher and receiver today, but noted it’s still early. Today was the 49ers’ first training camp practice. Wagoner’s notes seemed to indicate rookie RB Kaelon Black is in the No. 3 spot while veteran RB Patrick Taylor Jr. sits at No. 4. Things can change quickly, but today’s report backs up what we catalogued here from March through May — that James is next up behind starting RB Christian McCaffrey. He is a worthwhile late-round dart throw in summer drafts right now.-Nic Bodiford
